full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party no. 1 
to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 07.01.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 529 of 2002 reversing those dated 29.08.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 165 of 1992 dismissing the suit shall not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the 'Rule, in a nutshell, can be stated thus, the present opposite party no. 1 as plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No. 165 of 1992 in the 4th  Court of learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka against the defendant-petitioner and pro-forma-opposite party no. 02 for specific performance of contract contending inter alia that the defendant no. 01 Mosammat Zabun Nessa Begum, wife of Din Mohammad Khan is the owner of the suit land and while she proposed to sale the land the plaintiff agreed at a consideration of Tk. 3,60,000/- (three lacs sixty thousand). The defendant no. 01 executed a contract for sale on 10.07.1990 after receiving a sum of Tk. 50,000/-(fifty thousand) as advance money and thereafter, on 11.07.1990 the defendant no. 01 received Tk. 60,000/- (sixty thousand) and on 12.07.1990 received Tk. 50,000/-(fifty thousand) and in this way she received Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac sixty thousand) from the plaintiff. The plaintiff after that went abroad and appointed his wife Rokeya Begum attorney to deal with the matter. Rokeya Begum thereafter executed another deed of contract with the defendant no. 01 on 11 .12.1991 relinquishing their previous contract on a condition that if the defendant no. 01 failed to repay the money within 21.03.1992 which she received as per deed of contract for sale dated 10.07.1990 she would execute and register the kabala deed and failing which the plaintiff will get the kabala deed registered through court. The further case of the plaintiff is such that on 13.03.1992 and 17.03.1992 the defendant no. 01 promised to execute the kabala deed but on 21.03.1992 she refused to execute the same. Thereafter, the plaintiff on 29.03.1992 served legal notice upon the defendant and lastly; filed the original suit for specific performance of contract. 

3. The contrary case of the defendant no. 01 in short, is such that on 10.07.1990 she entered into a contract with the plaintiff and received Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) and thereafter, the defendant no. 01 requested the plaintiff for getting the kabala registered after paying the rest consideration money. On 27.11.1990 the defendant no. 01 served a legal notice upon the plaintiff but the plaintiff did not receive the same. Thereafter, the defendant no. 01 served another legal notice on 31.01.1991 upon the uncle of the plaintiff and upon his guardian Abu Hanif but they did not receive the said notice. On 03.04.1991 the son of the defendant also sent a legal notice to Abu Hanif and on 10.04.1991 Abu Hanif in his reply stated that he did not receive any notice. Thereafter, Md. Ismail Khan on several occasions met with the plaintiff to communicate with Abu Hanif but Abu Hanif dragged time without paying the rest amount. On 10.05.1991 the plaintiff served a legal notice upon the defendant no. 01 and the defendant no. 01 gave her reply on 28.04.1991. The plaintiff in reply requested the defendant no. 01 to return his consideration money by a letter dated 13.05.1991 and thereafter, both the parties executed an agreement contract on 11.12.1991. As per terms of that contract the plaintiff would have receive the money back and the defendant no. 01 would collect the money by selling the suit property but the plaintiff did not come to receive back the money on that date although the defendant no. 01 was ready to pay the amount. The plaintiff without taking back the consideration money served legal notice and the defendant through her lawyer gave reply to that. Subsequently the plaintiff on false allegation filed the original suit out of ill motive. 

4. During trial of the original suit both the parties adduced 3(three) witnesses each including documentary evidence and the learned trial court after hearing by his judgment and decree dated 27.04.2002 dismissed the suit on contest. Being aggrieved the plaintiff preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Dhaka being Title Appeal No. 529 of 2002 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge. 2nd Court, Dhaka and the learned appellate court below by the impugned judgment and decree dated 07.01.2010 allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree of the learned court of appeal the defendant-respondent-petitioner has preferred this revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 

6. During hearing of this revisional application Mr. Md. Ekramul Islam and Mr. Md. Badiuzzaman, the learned advocates appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Mahbubay Alam and Mr. Mohammad Shah Alam, the learned advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 

7. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of .the appeal committed illegality and failed to consider the merit of the original suit and in sifting the onus of proving the case the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned advocate further submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal failed to assess the evidence on record properly in its true perspective and also failed to consider the deposition of the witnesses rightly and as such committed error of law. The plaintiff to the suit during trial of the original suit failed to discharge his onus in proving the case specially the terms of the admitted contract between the parties to have the relief as prayed for and the trial court rightly during disposal of the original suit after proper assessment of evidence dismissed the suit due to failure of the plaintiff to prove his case but in the subsequent appeal the lower appellate court arbitrarily without assessing the evidence properly and appreciating the actual position of law reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and decreed the suit. The learned advocate on behalf of the petitioner also submits that the plaintiff to the suit is totally failed to prove by tangible, credible evidence that the defendant has failed to return the money within the stipulated time. By the supplementary deed of contract between the parties the onus of proving the plea that the defendant has failed to repay the amount not proved. The conditions of the subsequent agreement would have to prove by the 
plaintiff and it is the basis of the plaintiff's claim to get the decree but the plaintiff failed to prove that onus. The plaintiff's witnesses failed to establish the condition nos. 3 and 4 of the deed of the agreement dated 11.12.1991 but on the other hand by series of legal notices the case of the defendants is proved. The learned advocate lastly submits that violation of the conditions of Exhibit-`Gha' i.e. the deed of agreement dated 11.12. I991 can be a ground for the plaintiff to get the relief prayed, but it is not proved and in fixing the burden of proof the learned appellate court below is totally misconceived and instead of the plaintiff the learned Additional District Judge, 211(1 Court, Dhaka fixed the burden on the defendant arbitrarily while the trial court rightly fixed the burden of proof on the plaintiff which is not proved at-all. Within the pleading of the plaintiff in his plaint the existence of the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 is absent and as such the plaint is vague and unspecified where as the entire case of the plaintiff depends upon violation of the conditions cited within the contents of the deed dated 11.12.1991 marked as Exhibit- `Ga'. Despite the plaintiff failed to prove the violation of conditions of Exhibit-'Ga' the learned lower appellate court decreed the suit in his favour which is perverse and not under the ambit of relevant laws. It is not proved by any evidence that the defendant has failed to repay the amount 1,60,000/- (one lac and sixty thousand) by the stipulated time as mentioned within the condition of the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991. The learned counsel on behalf of the petitioner submits that the defendant have no subsisting interest in the land of agreement as the defendant with the consent of the plaintiff sold out the property in favour of 3rd party who after his purchase mutated his name and subsequently transferred the suit land in favour of 4th party which is mentioned by the defendants in where pleading within the written statement. 

8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverts the argument advanced from the side of the learned advocate for the petitioner and submits that the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and rightly held that the trial court during disposal of the original suit committed error of law as well as facts and in deciding the fate of the suit there has been miscourage of justice. Considering the said aspect the appellate court below after proper sifting of evidence and consideration of facts decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellant rightly and after the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff have already obtained the kabala deed registered through court. The learned advocate further submits that by supplementary agreement the onus of proving the respective plea of the defendant has been sifted to her that she tried to give the money back within the stipulated time as mentioned within the content of the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 marked as Exhibit-`Ga'. Admittedly the .defendant received a sum of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) from the plaintiff and it is the incumbent duty upon the defendant to establish her case by cogent, competent credible evidence that she ever tried to return the money back to the plaintiff within the time specified in the content of the document which is a admitted deed of agreement between the parties. The learned advocate for the opposite party also submits that admittedly the original deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 after its signing was kept within the custody of the defendant which is the backbone of the suit. It is the definite condition within the document that the sum of Tk. 1,60,000/4one lac and sixty thousand) is to be refunded by the defendant in favour of the plaintiff within 21.03.1992 but the defendant has failed to prove that she ever made any effort to refund the amount in favour of the plaintiff. The learned advocate lastly submits that by execution of second agreement the terms -and conditions of the first agreement have become redundant and in consultation with the evidence on record properly the learned appellate court below rightly held that the fact of returning the amount or any effort to repay the amount by the defendant within the stipulated time not at-all proved rather disproved by the defendant's witnesses. The witness no. 2 for the defendant Ismail Khan is totally silent about the second agreement while it is the case of the defendant that through him the defendant tried to repay the amount by 21.03.1992. Apart from this: this witness Ismail Khan did not corroborate the witness no. 01 of the defendant on the specific case that she (defendant) tried to repay the amount in favour of the plaintiff. Besides this, the witness no. 03 for the plaintiff Haji Hanif did not corroborate the defendant's case that the son of the defendant i.e. the witness no. 02 for the defendant ever went before him with money on 21.03.1992. Under Section 103 of the Evidence Act the burden of proof is entirely lies upon the defendant and the lower appellate court rightly observed in his findings that in discharging the onus the defendant has hopelessly failed and that the plaintiff has successfully proved his bonafide. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party taking notice of the case record argued that no legal notice was given to the plaintiff for taking the money in between 11.12.1991 to 21.03.1992. Lastly; there is no misrepresentation of facts, non-consideration of material evidence and misreading or non-reading of evidence from the side of the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka during disposal of the appeal by which it can be held that any error of law was done by the lower appellate court in passing the impugned judgment and decree and as such there is nothing to interfere with the same. 

9. Heard the learned advocates of both sides, perused the case records, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 

10. On perusal of the case record it transpires that admittedly the defendant was the owner of the disputed property and there was an agreement for sale in respect of the disputed property on 10.07.1990 at a consideration of Tk. 3,60,000/-(three lacs and sixty thousand). It is also an admittedly position that out of the total consideration amount the defendant no. 01 received Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) from the plaintiff. It was a condition within the deed of agreement initially that taking the remaining amount of Tk. 2,00.000/- (two lacs) the defendant no. 01 will execute and register a sub-kabala deed within 3(three) months. Admittedly the kabala was not executed and registered by the defendant within the time after receiving the remaining amount of consideration and meanwhile, the plaintiff went abroad after executing a power of attorney. The wife of the plaintiff became the attorney of the plaintiff who entered into a second agreement with the defendant on 11.12.1991 marked as exhibit-`Ga' and in that agreement there was a condition that by 21.03.1992 the defendant will repay the amount in favour of the plaintiff which was taken by her and in that case only it was an under taking from the side of the plaintiff that his claim would be frustrated to get the kabala deed registered. It was agreed by the defendant no. 01 that if she fails to pay the money to the plaintiff within the stipulated time mentioned above she would execute and register a sub-kabala deed in favour of the plaintiff after taking the balance consideration amount. 

11. In view of the above facts of the case we have come-across from the documentaly evidence that by supplementary agreement deed dated 11.12.1991 the initial contract between the parties has become redundant. In this context; it is obvious to note that the burden of proof which was initially fixed upon the plaintiff has been obviously sifted upon the defendant by the very inception of the supplementary deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 marked as exhibit-'Gha' and in this regard; it is the positive case of the defendant-petitioner that she offered the sum of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) which was admittedly taken by her to the plaintiff by the stipulated time but the plaintiff refused to accept the same. 

12. In respect of the claim and counter claim of the respective parties to the suit consulting the relevant papers specially the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties it is apparent from the face of the papers that in support of the respective case the plaintiff to the suit examined 3(three) witnesses while the defendant adduced the same number of
witnesses in support of her pleading. The witness no. 01 for the plaintiff is Md. Jahid Hossain who deposed on behalf of the plaintiff as "আম-মোক্তার". It was stated by this witness in his deposition that the plaintiff appointed his wife attorney to conduct the case and the attorney of the plaintiff entered into a second agreement with the defendant on 11.12.1991 and it was a recital within the document that the amount which has already been paid would have to be return on or before 21.03.1992. This witness in his deposition states supporting the pleading of the plaintiff and denied the suggestion given to him from the side of the defendant. The witness no. 2 is the plaintiff to the suit Md. Hossain Ahmed. In his deposition he states about the existence of "আম-মোক্তার নামা” given by him in favour of witness no. 01 Jahid Hossain and prior to that he executed the other "আম-মোক্তার নামা” in the name of his wife. The last witness for the plaintiff is Haji Abu Hanif. This witness states about the deed of agreement dated 10.07.1990 in which he is a witness. The said deed is marked as 'exhibit-2'. From his deposition it appears that the  defendant received a sum of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) out , of the total consideration of Tk. 3,60,000/- (three lacs and sixty thousand). This witness was also present on the date of subsequent deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991. He denied that, pursuant to the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 the son of the defendant no. 01 Ismail Khan went to his residence on 22.03.1992. Vis-à-vis; the witness no.01 for the defendants is doctor Md. Soyeb Khan who is the son of the defendant Most. Zabun Nessa Begum. By virtue of an "আম-মোক্তার নামা” to conduct the case on behalf of her mother he deposed supporting the case of the defendant. As regard the terms of agreement this witness in his cross-examination states at a stage, 
‘‘২১/৩/৯২ ইং তাং বাদীপক্ষ হইতে ঐ টাকা নেওয়ার জন্য কেহ আসেন নাই। অতঃপর বিবাদীর পুত্র মোঃ ইসমাইল খান টাকা দেওয়ার জন্য বাদীর বাড়ীতে যান। বাদীকে না পাইয়া তাহার ভাতিজা আবু হানিফের সাথে দেখা করার জন্য তাহার অফিসে যান। কেন টাকা নেন নাই এই প্রশ্নের জবাবে আবু হানিফ বলেন যে, বাদী ও তাহার স্ত্রী কী করিবে সে সম্পর্কে চিন্তা ভাবনা করিতেছে। 

13. The witness no. 02 of the defendant-petitioner Ismail Khan who is the son of the defendant no. 01 without corroborating their previous witness Soyeb Khan states about the initial deed of agreement dated 10.07.1990 and payment of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) out of the total consideration of Tk. 3,60,000/-(three lacs and sixty thousand). The last witness of the defendant Md. Arif Ahmed Chowdhury also states only in his deposition about the conditions imposed within the content of the initial deed of agreement and in his cross-examination he denied that he was not present at the time of deed of agreement between the parties. 

14. Going through the evidence on record it is apparent that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal fixing the onus of proof upon the defendant no. 01 to show that she offered Tk. 1,60,000/- (one lac and sixty thousand) to the plaintiff on or before 21.03.1992 held that the defendant has failed to discharge the onus that she ever offered the amount in favour of the plaintiff by the stipulated time and in this context; I have every reason to incline such a view that by the execution of second agreement paper the responsibility has been sifted upon the defendant to discharge the onus in proving that she ever tried to repay the amount which was admittedly taken by her from the plaintiff. Under Section 103 of the Evidence Act the lower appellate court was quite justified in holding that the onus of proving the fact that the defendant tried to repay the amount lies upon her. On perusal of the plaint it transpires that, it has been clearly stated therein that the terms of the contract was not complied with by the defendant-petitioner and having failed to get the kabala deed registered after its execution from the defendant the plaintiff filed the original suit for specific performance of contract. 

15. In a suit for specific performance of contract the provisions laid down in Section 12 of the Specific Relief Act is to be followed. The spirit of relevant law is such that the specific performance of contract may in the discretion of the court be enforced when the act agreed to be done is in the performance, wholly or partly, of a trust. In the instant case as we have come-across from the pleading of the parties that it is a fact that the fate of the plaintiff's suit depends on the violation of the terms of contract between the parties pursuant to an agreement executed on 11.12.1991 marked as Exhibit- `Ga'. From the creation of the aforesaid deed of agreement the money which was paid is required to be repaid by the defendant within a stipulated period but in the instant case obviously as I have stated earlier that the defendant who admittedly received the amount has failed to discharge her responsibility in proving that she repaid the amount or ever tried to repay the same. It is to be noted here that by the execution of the second agreement the terms of first agreement has become infructuous and it is within the record that there is a condition incorporated within the content of the document that the amount paid in favour of the defendant by the plaintiff will have to repay in plaintiff's favour by the defendant by 21.03.1992. The defendant-respondent-petitioner Mosammat Zabun Nessa Begum did not depose in the instant suit but on her behalf her attorney doctor Md. Soyeb Khan as defendant's witness no. 1 tried to establish the specific contention to the effect that by the stipulated time they tried to repay the amount in favour of the plaintiff but the plaintiff refused to accept the same and thereafter the son of the defendant Md. Ismail Khan with a sum of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) went to the residence of the plaintiff but in absence of the plaintiff the defendant's son met his nephew Abu Hanif at his office and Abu Hanif did not receive the amount. In this regard; the most important witness is Md. Ismail Khan who deposed on behalf of the defendant's case but it is curious to note that this witness not at-all corroborated the case of the defendant and the statement of the defendant's witness no. 01 as to the fact of rendering money in favour of the plaintiff pursuant to the deed of agreement marked Exhibit-`Ga' not supported by this witness Ismail. The witness no. 03 of the plaintiff Haji Abu Hanif also not supported the proposition that the son of the defendant went before him with money on 21.03.1992. There is no corroborative, credible tangible evidence in support of the aforesaid contention that the defendant ever paid the money or offered the money which was taken by her as partial consideration of the total amount of Tk. 3,60,000/- (three lacy and sixty thousand). 

16. Upon the pleadings of the parties the evidence adduced go to show that the plaintiff's witnesses by their testimony corroborated the case of the plaintiff as to the existence of the deed of agreement payment of partial consideration amount and non-payment of the amount from the side of the vendor in favour of the vendee which was accepted by her pursuant to the initial deed of agreement. The legal notices marked as Exhibits- '3' and '4' also supports the case of the plaintiff and the witnesses who deposed except some minor discrepancies corroborated the plaint case in tow which is properly assessed and evaluated by the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal. The legal notices which were sent by the plaintiff in favour of the defendants also proves his bonafide and as such the onus of proving the plaintiff's case has been successfully discharged by tangible evidence on record which was considered during deciding the merit of the appeal rightly. Hence, obviously the plaintiff to the suit has done his part as per agreement and was also willing to repay the balance consideration. But in the instant case the part of proof i.e. the burden of proof which was imposed upon the defendant by the very execution of the second deed of agreement dated 11.12.1 991 not proved rather disproved. 

17. Under Section 12 of the Specific Relief Act which is the relevant law of this case and the provisions of law by which the case will govern lies in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party since it has proved that the plaintiff has done his part as per agreement and was also willing to repay the balance consideration money with a view to get the sale deed registered. 

18. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the defendant-petitioner was duty bound to perform her part but has failed. Hence; consulting the impugned judgment and decree along with the judgment and decree passed by the trial court I have nothing but to hold such a view that the lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed no wrong in deciding the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellant. No such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts is noticed by which it can be held that out of misconception and non-consideration of facts the lower appellate court arrived at a decision that the suit for specific performance of contract is liable to be decreed. The findings of fact whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate court being the last and final court of facts is immune from interference in the revisional jurisdiction of this court unless it is shown that the decisions have been based upon gross misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice or those have been founded on misconception or misinterpretation of any document or otherwise perverse contrary to law, evidence and materials on record. In the instant case; as I have already stated earlier that no such illegality is noticed by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. As regard alleged purchase deeds of the subsequent purchaser-3rd party-petitioners it is needless to advert that in absence of valid right to transfer by their venders their so-called purchase deeds are nothing but mere paper transactions having no legal sanction and accordingly they acquired no right to property. 

19. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and evidence referred to above I'm constrained to hold such a view that the Rule have got no substance to succeed.
 
20. In the result; the Rule is discharged.

21. The impugned judgment and decree dated 07.01.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 529 of 2002 reversing those dated 29.08.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No: 165 of 1992 dismissing the suit is hereby affirmed. 

22. The order of stay granted earlier by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

23. However, there will be no order as to costs. 

24. Communicate the judgment and order at-once to the court concerned for information and necessary action. 

25. Send back the Lower Court's Record immediately. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 26.11.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.416 of 2004.)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J. This Civil Petition for leave to appeal, at the instance, of the plaintiff-respondent, has been directed against the judgment and order dated 26.11.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 416 of 2004 making the Rule absolute.

2. The present plaintiff-petitioner along with some others instituted the Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chirirbandar, Dinajpur for a declaration that the preliminary decree as well as the final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 are illegal, ineffective and inoperative, making allegations to the effect that summons and notices of that partition suit were not served upon them, that Dhali Bibi the plaintiff of that partition suit had no subsisting interest in the divisible land, that the purchasers were not made parties in that partition suit and that the defendants who were of unsound mind and were minors were not represented properly in that partition suit.

3. That Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 was contested by saham-praying defendants of Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 by filing written statement. The case of the contesting defendants was that the summons and notices of that Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 were duly served upon the defendants and the suit was decreed on contest and the Advocate Commissioner partitioned the property and prepared the saham after serving notices upon the defendants duly and the preliminary decree was made final lawfully as no objection was filed against the Advocate Commissioner's report and that the final decree was executed by filing Partition Execution Case No. 1 of 1988 and possession of land was delivered on 28.03.1988 and that Dhali Bibi has been possessing the suit Land on the strength of her right and title.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties, decreed that Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 holding only that in the Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 the present plaintiffs were not served with the summons and notices. Against that judgment of the trial court the contesting defendants preferred Other Appeal No. 53 of 1991 before the learned District Judge, Dinajpur, which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dinajpur. The appellate court dismissed the appeal, affirming the judgment of the trial court making observation to the effect that the plaintiffs were able to prove their case that they were not informed about that partition suit and that the trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs, rightly declared the preliminary decree and the final decree of the Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 illegal and inoperative.

5. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the appellate court the contesting defendants filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division ultimately made the Rule absolute setting aside the judgments of both the courts below and consequently dismissing the Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989.

6. The plaintiff-petitioner has challenged the legality and propriety of this judgment of the revisional court by filing this civil petition for leave to appeal.

7. We have heard Mr. Giusuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and also Mr. A. H. M. Mushfiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 to 6.

8. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has argued that both the courts of fact, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the, plaintiffs, found that the summons and notices, of the original partition suit were not served upon the plaintiffs and consequently both the courts rightly found the preliminary decree as well as the final decree passed in that Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 illegal. That the trial court being the first court of fact and the appellate court below being the final court of facts their concurrent findings as to non-service of summons upon the defendants in the original partition suit cannot be interfered by the revisional court in the absence of any misreading or non-reading or misinterpretation of the evidence on record by those two courts below. The learned Advocate has argued that the High Court Division has committed illegality in setting aside the concurrent findings of the courts of fact. The learned Advocate has argued further that in this suit for declaring the judgment and decree of the earlier partition suit illegal the onus was upon the contesting defendants to prove that summons and notices of the partition suit were duly served upon the plaintiffs of the present suit, but the contesting defendants did not take any step or initiative to discharge that onus and in the circumstances, the evidence of the P.Ws. were sufficient to prove that the summons and notices of the original partition suit were not served upon them.

9. Mr. A. H. M. Mushfiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 1-6 has made submission supporting the impugned judgment of the High Court Division.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the judgments of the trial court, the appellate court and the revisional court.

<u>11. It appears that before the trial court seven witnesses were examined from the side of the plaintiffs all of whom were defendants in the original partition suit. These 7 P.Ws. deposed before the court to the effect only that they did not get summons and notices of the original partition suit. Save and except the evidence of these 7 P.Ws. who are most interested witnesses the plaintiffs did not or could not adduce any other evidence or facts or material to substantiate their allegation that the summons and notices of the original partition suit were not served upon them and these were suppressed collusively. It appears that the trial court and also the appellate court relying on this evidence of the P.Ws. only declared the preliminary and final decree passed in that partition suit illegal.</u>

<u>12. But the High Court Division, on careful and meticulous examination of the evidence and materials on record, pointed out that no necessary evidence or materials were produced before the courts below to substantiate the allegation of non-service of summons and notices; that neither the record of Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 was proved before the courts below, inn the service return of that partition suit was admitted into evidence for the purpose of proving this allegation of non-service of summons and notices. The High Court Division, on consideration of the evidence on record, observed also that the evidence of P.Ws. failed to make out any case of collusion in obtaining the preliminary decree and final decree passed in that partition suit. The High Court Division further, detected that the defendant No. 1 of that partition suit named Badiuzzaman along with some other defendants submitted written statement in that partition suit and this defendant No. 1 Badiuzzaman is the full brother of the plaintiff No. 1 of the present Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 and he has also deposed in that suit as P. W.2 in favour of the plaintiffs. On consideration of these facts and circumstances and the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2-which have been quoted in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division the High Court Division made comment to the effect that this P.W.2 Badiuzzaman, in fact, filed this present suit setting up his sister as plaintiff.</u>

<u>13. On going through the judgments of both the courts of facts we do not find any wrong in the above findings of the High Court Division. From the judgment of the courts below it appears that in the original partition suit the defendant No. 1 Badiuzzaman (who deposed in the present suit as P. W.2) along with some other defendants submitted written statement and this very fact has not been denied by this defendant No. 1 while deposing in this present suit for setting aside the decree of that earlier partition suit as P.W.2. In the circumstances where the own brother of the plaintiff No. 1 of the present suit got summons and notices of the earlier partition suit and also appeared in that partition suit and filed written statement and where, admittedly, some other defendants also contested in that partition suit and prayed saham, it is hard to believe that the other defendants of that partition suit-who are full sister and other close relations of the contesting defendants did not get summons and notices of that partition suit or did not know about that partition suit.</u>

<u>14. In this circumstance the mere statements of the P.Ws. that they did not get summons and notices of the original partition suit are not sufficient at all for setting aside the judgment and decree passed by a court of law. When a judgment and decree is passed by court of law it is presumed that this judgment and decree was passed in accordance with law by following all the requirements of law so long it is not proved by cogent evidence that these judgment and decree were obtained collusively suppressing the summons and notices. In the present case the preliminary decree as well as the final decree of Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 was passed by a competent court of law. So the onus to prove this preliminary and final decree collusive or illegal was on the plaintiffs of the present suit who alleged the same. But the plaintiffs of this present suit could not produce any evidence at all to prove any collusion or fraud in obtaining the impugned decree of the partition suit. They did not take any step or initiative to bring the record of the Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 before the trial court for the purpose of proving that the summons and notices were not issued and served or these were suppressed Collusively. None of the witnesses named in the service return of that partition suit also was produced before the trial court by the plaintiffs to deny the service of summons and notices in his presence and thereby to support the plaintiffs case that the summons and notices of the original partition Suit were not actually served upon them. In the circumstances, the mere assertion of the plaintiffs that they did not get any summons and notices of the partition suit was not at all sufficient for holding that actually the summons and notices of that partition suit were not served upon the plaintiffs of the present suit specially in the circumstances where it was sufficiently disclosed before the trial court that the own brother of the plaintiff No. 1 and some other defendants of that partition suit got summons and notices of that partition suit and they also appeared in that partition suit, filed written statement and contested.</u>

<u>15. In the circumstances the High Court Division rightly found that the plaintiffs of the present suit could not prove their case that the preliminary and final decree passed in the Partition Suit No.194 of 1984 were obtained collusively by suppressing summons and notices. The High Court Division rightly observed also that the courts below without applying judicial mind set aside the hard-earned preliminary and final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984.</u>

16. We find no reason to interfere with the above findings and observations of the High Court Division. Rather, considering the facts and circumstances stated above we find that the High Court Division rightly set aside the judgment of both the courts below and rightly dismissed the suit.

17. Evidently, there is no merit in this leave petition and hence it is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 03.12.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 6721 and 6690 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J:- These two leave petitions have been filed by the same petitioner and are in between the same parties and have arisen out of a common judgment and order dated 3.12.2007 passed in Civil Revision Nos. 6721 and 6690 of 2002, heard and disposed of, by a Single Bench of the High Court Division, making the rules absolute. 

2. The Civil Revision No. 6721 of 2002 arises out of the common judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 106.of 2000 preferred by the defendant-respondents hereof, heard and disposed of along with cross appeal filed in the said appeal by the plaintiff-petitioners here-of. dismissing the appeal, and that the Civil Revision No. 6690 of 2002 arose against allowing the cross appeal, vide judgment and decree dated 29.10.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Jhalokathi, modifying the decree passed by the trial Court. Both the Title Appeal No. 106 of 2000 and the cross appeal arose out of the same judgment and decree dated 28.5.2000 passed in Title Suit No. 28 of A- 1997 by the learned Assistant Judge, Nalchiti, Jhalokathi, decreeing the suit in part. 

3. The petitioners hereof, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No.28 of 1997 for partition praying for a saham of 13 decimals of land out of 31 decimals of land in Hal-Dad; No. 205 of S.A. Khatian No. 791/144/544 of Mouja-Nalchiti under J. L. No. 43 of Nalchiti Police Station, District-Jhalokhati, detailed in schedule-Ka of the plaint, contending, amongst others, that the plaintiff No. 2 became owner and possessor of 61/2 decimals of land vide registered sale deed dated 27.7.1967 from Hatem Ali Sharif and the plaintiff No.1 became owner and possessor of 61/2 decimals of land by registered heba deed dated 17.2.1993 from Hatem Ali Sharif. The said 13 decimals of land was duly recorded in the records of right in the name of Hatem Ali Sahrif in Plot No. 205 of S.A. Khatian No. 791 under Mouja-Nalchiti, J.L. No. 43 under Nalchiti Police Station and thus the plaintiff-petitioner were owning and possessing the said 13 decimals of land and enjoying usufruct therefrom, since the respective transfers, on payment of rates, taxes and other charges to the Revenue office. 

4. The defendant Nos.1-4 are the successors-in-interest from the recorded owners of S.A. Khatian No. 544 and the defendant No. 5 is the successor-in-interest of the record of tenant of S.A. Khatian No. 144 and the said defendants on 20th Poush, 1403 13.S. denied to make amicable partition of the suit land which were being possessed and enjoyed by the respective parties with-out partition in metes and bounds i.e. on proper measurement. 

5. The defendant-respondent Nos. 1 -4 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that they inherited the property from their predecessor-in-interest, Copal Chandra, who inherited the properties of his brother-Makhon Lal on his death. Hatem Ali Sharif, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, owned and possessed only 83/4 decimals of land in Plot Nos. 197 and 198 by purchase from Makhon Lal but in the records of right 13 decimals of land in Plot No.205 is shown against the name of Hatem Ali Sharif incorrectly in place of 83A decimals of land, and that in Title Suit No. 59 of 1992 filed by said Hatem Ali Sharif and others, as plaintiffs, for partition and Hatem Ali Sharif prayed for a saham of 213/4 decimals of land, and the said suit was ho\\ e \ el decreed, allowing said Hatem Ali Shutt a saham of 83/4 decimals of land, and that in the said partition suit, the plaintiff Nos. l and 2 of the instant case were made defendant Nos. 6 and 7 respectably, showing their ownership and passion in respect of 13 decimals of land each owning and possessing 61/2 decimates of land vide sale deed dated 27.07.1967 and heba deed dated 17.02.1993. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

6. The trial Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record decreed the suit in part allowing a saham of only 83/4 decimals of land in Plot No. 205 out of 13 decimals, since prayed for. 

7. Being aggrieved there-against the defendant Nos. 1-4, as appellants, preferred Title Appeal No. 106 of 2000 in the Court of District Judge, Jhalokathi, challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 28 of 1997 against allowing the saham of 83/4 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiffs and praying for dismissal of the suit. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 28 of 1997 filed a cross appeal in the said appeal praying for a decree for saham for entire 13 decimals of land, as prayed for in the original suit, on modification of the saham allotted by the impugned judgment and decree passed by the court below. 

8. The appellate Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties dismissed the appeal of the defendant-appellants and allowed the cross appeal of the plaintiff-respondents observing, amongst others, that in the records of right 13 decimals of land in Plot No. 205 stands in the name of Hatem Ali Sharif and the said record of right was never challenged or corrected and that said Hatem All Sharif transferred 61/2 decimals of land out of the said 13 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff No. 2 by a registered sale deed dated 27.07.1967 and subsequently transferred by way of gift rest 61/2 decimals of said land in favour of the plaintiff No. 1 hereof by a deed dated 17.02.1993, and that the said Hatem Ali Sharif and thereafter the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 respectively have been paying rates and taxes in respect of said 13 decimals of land and enjoying usufructs therefrom without any objection from any quarter. The appellate Court further observed that though the certified copy of the judgment and decree passed in Partition Suit No. 59 of 1992 has been produced but neither copy of the Advocate Commissioner's report nor any document in support of actual partition by the Commissioner and or delivery thereof were produced in Court and as such there is no proof of execution of the decree passed in the said partition suit. The appellate Court further observed that though the defendant-appellants claimed the ownership and possession of their mother, Rani Bala, in respect of 26 decimals of land beyond the Makhan Lars land, and the ownership and possession of Gopal Chandra, the alleged brother of Mahon Lal, but no documentary proof could be produced before the Court and as such the appellate Court did not believe the ownership and possession of the said Rani Bala and Gopal Chandra as alleged and accordingly dismissed the appeal and allowed the cross-appeal. Being aggrieved against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed in dismissing the appeal and allowing the cross appeal, the defendants filed the Civil Revision Nos. 6721 and 6690 of 2002 respectively. 

9. The High Court Division heard both the Rules, as issued in the aforesaid revision cases, and disposed of the same by a common judgment dated 03.12.2007 making both the Rules absolute and thereby dismissed the Title Suit No. 28 of 1997, relying on the saham allowed in favour of plaintiff-Hat-Ali Sharif in the earlier partition suit being Title Suit No. 59 of 1992 and in view of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1992 held that the Title Suit No. 28 of 1997 is hit by the principle of res-judicata and the Courts below committed gross error of law in overlooking the aspect of res-judicata and thereby judgment and decree passed by the courts below were based on erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice. 

10. We have perused the leave petition and heard the learned Advocate. We have also perused the impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division as well as the judgments passed by the courts below. The learned Advocate submitted that the High Court Division acted illegally in not taking into consideration that the appellate court below after scrutiny of the Exhibits-'Ka', 'Ka-1', 'Ka-2' and 'Ka-3', which are certified copies of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1992, has held that the properties in reference as well as the parties of Title Suit No. 28 of 1997 and Title Suit No. 59 of 1992 were not same and similar. The learned Advocate further sub-mitted that in the earlier partition suit, being Title Suit No. 59 of 1992, Hatem Ali Sharif, as plaintiff No.1, claimed 213/4 acres of land asserting, amongst others, that he has transferred 13 decimals of land in favour of the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 of Title Suit No.59 of 1992, who are plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 in the instant suit i.e. Title Suit No. 28 of 1997, and that on consideration of the materials and evidence on record the said Court decreed a saham of 83/4 decimals of land in favour of the said Hatem Ali Sharif in Title Suit No. 59 of 1992 and thereby it appears that Hatem Ali Sharif was not given decree for rest 13 decimals of land, which also goes to show that the said court considered the transfer of 13 decimals of land made by Hatem Ali Sharif in favour of the plain-tiffs hereof, who were defendant Nos. 6 and 7 in the said partition suit, and the said decree as passed allowing saham of 83/4 decimals in favour of Hatem Ali Sharif appears to be in accordance with law. The learned Advocate further sub-mitted that there being no issue of res-judicata before the trial Court the findings of the High Court Division on such issue, without affording any opportunity to the parties to address the said issue in accordance with law, cannot be sustained, and that We allocation of saham being a finding of fad:, based on documents and other evidences on record, and the same being finding by the appellate court below, the last court of finding of fact on consideration of the materials and evidence on record, the High Court Division erred in interfering with such findings of facts in its revisional jurisdiction in the absence of any allegation of non-consideration of any evidence on record or any perverse finding. Our Appellate Division has settled the principle that High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction normally will not interfere with the findings of fact of any appellate Court, even if the appreciation of the evidence appears to be erroneous. 

11. We find substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate and hence inclined to grant leave. 

12. Accordingly, Leave is granted to consider the ground Nos. 1,2 and 4 of both the leave petitions, which are as under: 
1. that a decree in a previous partition suit where it has not been executed does not bar a fresh suit for partition on a right to partition arising subsequently to the first suit, as to all points and refusal to settle a scheme for partition in a previous suit does not operate as a bar to a subsequent suit to have a scheme framed when the reasons arises at a later stage and without considering this vital legal aspect the High Court Division set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below miscarriage of justice; 
II. that the S.A. Khatian stands in the names of the plaintiffs which raised a presumption that the plain-tiffs are in possession of the suit land and thereby the decree granted by the lower appellate court in respect of 13 decimals of land does not suffer from any error of law and as such the learned Judge of the High Court Division without considering the appellate Court's judgment made the Rule absolute; 
IV. that the plaintiffs acquired title on the basis of their Kabala dated 27.07.1967 in respect of 61/2 decimals and also on the basis of a deed of hebabilewaz dated 17.02.1993 in respect of 61/2 lower appellate court committed no error of law in granting a decree in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of the entire .13 decimals of land. 

13. Security of Tk. 1,000/- is to be deposited within one month each of the cases. 

14. The petitioners are permitted to pre-pare the paper book out of Court in accordance with Rules. 

15. The appeals to be heard one after another. 

End.

Mr. M. Nurul Islam, J:- This rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 12.2.89 and 19.2.89 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge Court No. II, Bogra in partition appeal No, 182 of 1985 affirming those dated 25.9.85 and 2.11.85 respectively passed by the learned Munsif (Now Assistant Judge) Sherpur, District Bogra in partition suit No, 63 of 1984. 

	2. The fact giving rise to the plaintiffs case is that the suit jote originally belonged to one Chatu Sheikh and after his death his two sons Mohir Sheikh and Iman Sheikh inherited the suit jote in equal share and the C.S. record was pre-pared in their names. Mohir Sheikh died leaving on son Momtaz and two daughters Kasiran Bibi and Gedi. Iman Sheikh died leaving behind son Abdul Azim Kasiron died leaving son Kashem and one daughter Tuni Bibi. The petitioner purchased 2.26 decimals of land from Abdul Aziz son of 'man Sheikh and 41 decimals of land from Abdul Aziz and Kashem and 91 decimals of land from Kashern and Tuni Bibi by 3 registered Kabala dated 3.12.69. The petitioner while possessing the disputed land instituted a suit for permanent injunction bearing No. 131 of 1970 before the Munsif, 1st Court, Bogra against the opposite party for an area of 2.50 decimal of land out of the purchased land that suit was dismissed on contest on 26.12.76 with an observation that the plaintiff has got no title and possession in the suit property. The plaintiff, thereafter, in order to prefer an appeal against the judgment and decree of the aforesaid permanent injunction suit, engaged his tadbirkar Abdur Rahman Sheikh who gave him false information that he filed appeal but subsequently admitted that no such appeal was filed by him. Then the petitioner filed a partition suit being No. 63 of 1984 before the learned Munsif Sherpur, District Bogra and the suit was dismissed with the observation that the suit is barred by limitation and adverse possession and that the plaintiff i.e. the present petitioner has no title and possession in the disputed land according to the finding in the O.C. suit No. 131 of 1970. Against the judgment and decree of the partition suit the plaintiff preferred appeal before the District Judge, Bogra being appeal No. 182 of 1985. The said appeal was heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Court No. II, Bogra who by his judgment and decree dated 12.2.85 and 19.2.89 respectively dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. Being aggrieved at the decision the petitioner has filed this application and obtained the present rule. During pendency of the Rule the petitioner has filed an application before this court for amending the plaint of the partition suit No. 63 of 1984 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Sherpur, Bogra for adding a prayer for declaration of his title to the suit land. The opposite party has filed a counter affidavit denying the allegations made in the application for amendment and stated inter alia that the petitioner has got no title and possession in the disputed land and he has nothing to be aggrieved by the judgment and decree under challenge and that he has filed this suit only to cause suffering and harassment of the opposite parties. 

	3. The application for amendment was filed in this court on 15.2.93 and by an order dated 1.4.93 the said application was kept with the record as prayed for by the learned Advocate for the petitioner to be pressed at the time of hearing of the rule. 

	4. Mr. Md. Mozaffar Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner placed the application before me and submitted that the courts below has taken an erroneous view in dismissing the partition suit on the basis of the finding made in the permanent injunction suit of 1970. The Certified copy of the judgment of the afore-said partition suit marked as Ext. A shows that the learned Munsif framed an issue about petitioner's title and possession in the suit land and decided the issue against the petitioner. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the said issue is a redundant issue in the suit as in such suit the court can see the prima facie good title and existing possession of the suit land. So the decision on this issue cannot be res-judicata in the partition suit. 

	5. Mr, Shahid Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties vehemently opposes the argument put forward by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and submitted that the court decided this issue of title and possession of the suit land after taking evidence and discussing the same came to a clear finding in the matter, According to him the court below have rightly decided the suit for partition in view of the decision of the permanent injunction suit. 

	6. The record shows that the opposite party claimed title to the suit land on the basis of an auction purchase by the opposite party No. 1 for the share of Mohir Sheikh. Mohir Sheikh inherited half of the suit jote and his share was 2.262 decimals land. Share of Iman Sheikh has not been auction-sold. The opposite party took pat-tan of the land from the suit khatian from the auction purchaser and the petitioner purchased the share of Iman Sheikh and from disinterested heirs of Mohir Sheikh. The opposite party has claimed the share of Monir Sheikh. So, since the holding has not been partitioned amongst the co-sharer and both the parties are co-sharer of the suit properties and the permanent injunction suit generally cannot lie in such a holding as the petitioner filed the suit for injunction against co-sharer with a misconceived idea and the court decided the title of the suit property against him. In order to the decision the learned Advocate for the petitioner filed a petition for amendment of the plaint of the partition suit praying for declaration of title of the petitioner to the suit land. 

	7. In support of his prayer the learned Advocate has cited a decision in the case of Begum Fazilatunnessa vs. Nowshad Ali, reported in 29 DLR 314 wherein it was held follows:-
	"Rule of procedure is intended to act in aid of administration of justice-A party cannot be refused a just and legitimate relief merely because of some mistake in the pleadings due to inadvertence. The courts have always acted in aid of and to further the cause of justice and not to deny or frustrate it. Once the court is satisfied that the party was acting bonafide and by his mistake or omission he has not caused was in joy to the other side, there is no reason why the court should refuse a legitimate and just prayer to amend the pleadings. The view I have taken finds support from a decision of the Supreme Court of India in the case of Jai Ram Monohar Lal vs. National Building Material Supply, A.I.R. 1969. S.C. 1267 where it was held that how-ever negligent or careless may have been the omission, and however late the proposed amendment, the amendment may be allowed if it can be Made without any injustice to the other side." I have gone through the records and find that the petitioner prayed for partition of 2.262 decimals of land i.e. the share of his predecessor-in interest and that share has not been sold in auction. The opposite party will not suffer any injury if the amendment is allowed for proper adjudication of the suit. Since the opposite party has no claim over this portion of land. There was no such prayer before the courts below for amendment of the plaint. The courts below decided the partition suit on the basis of the title and possession decided in the suit for permanent injunction between the parties bearing No. 131 of 1970. 

	8. I have already observed about the permanent injunction suit against the co-sharer. Considering that view I find sub-stance in the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The judgment and decree of the courts below is also based on erroneous finding. 

	9. The rule is, accordingly, made absolute without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree passed by the courts below are set aside. The partition suit No. 63 of 1984 is sent back on remand for fresh trial after amending the plaint as per prayer of the petitioner. Send down the L.C. records at once. 

	End.
