Mr. Shahidul Islam, J.: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.4.1994 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, in Title Appeal No. 53 of 1991 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 10.1.1991 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, temporary additional Court, Faridpur, in Title Suit No. 753 of 1978 decreeing the suit in preliminary form but rejecting the prayer made under section 4 of the Partition Act. 

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule that the Petitioner as plaintiff instituted Suit No. 753 of 1978 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, temporary additional Court, Faridpur for a preliminary decree for partition to the extent of 8 annas share in the Ka schedule land to the plaint and seeking for pere-emption under section 4 of the Partition Act as against the Kha schedule land to the plaint measuring an area of 321/, decimals appertaining to plot No. 2523/2525 of mouja Raghunandanpur under Police Station Kotwali, District Faridpur contending, inter cilia, that the plaintiff and defendant No. 2 are the owners of schedule-Ka land to the plaint having 8 annas share each. The schedule Ka land to the plaint is an undivided ejmali homestead of the plaintiff and as well as of the defendant No. 2. The other land i.e. the land of plot No. 2525 is 'Matiul' land. The defendant No. 2 by a kabala deed dated 1 1.6.1975 sold the schedule Kha land to the plaint in favour of the defendant No. 1. There has been no partition by metes and bounds in respect of schedule-Ka land to the plaint. After purchase, the defendant No. I forcibly entered into the undivided homestead of the plaintiff and he made some constructions creating inconvenience to the plaintiffs peaceful possession in the said homestead. For convenience of possession the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 used to live separately by erecting homestead and began to possess in ejmali. There having arisen inconvenience of the plaintiffs possession he demanded partition by metes and bounds but the defendant No. 1 and 2 refused to do so and as such the suit. 

3. It is the further case of the plaintiff that the schedule Kha land to the plaint is a part and parcel of the undivided dwelling house and as such he is entitled to purchase the same under section 4 of the Partition Act. It is stated that the plaintiff is a Hindu by casts and the defendant No. 1 is a Mohammedan by faith. It is stated that it would be inconvenient and on the part of the plaintiff to live jointly with the defendant No. 1. It is the further case of the plaintiff that the persons who are residing in the Kha schedule homestead on behalf of the defendant No. 1 are not dealing with him properly and their activities have made his living in the homestead impossible. It is asserted that the defendant No. 1 is trying to evict the plaintiff from his homestead and exercising some unlawful activities upon the family members of the plaintiffs. There is no demarcation between the houses of the plaintiff and of the defendant No. 2 and the suit homestead is standing upon the plot No. 2523 as being the ancestral undivided homestead of the plaintiff and of the defendant No. 2. The defendant No. 2 sold Kha schedule land in favour of the defendant No. 1 beyond the knowledge of the plaintiff. The Kha schedule land being a part of undivided homestead of the plaintiff, he is entitled to get the same by pre-emption under section 4 of the Partition Act. With these averments he filed the suit. 

4. The defendant No. I contested the suit by filing a Written Statement denying the plaint's case and contending, inter cilia, that he purchased the Kha schedule land to the plaint within the knowledge of the plaintiff. The defendant asked the plaintiff to purchase the suit land but the latter requested the defendant to purchase the same accepting him to by a good neighbored. After purchase, he filled in the same by earth. It is his case that the kha schedule land is separated from the 'ka' land and he constructed a tin shaded homestead upon the said land. He constructed a latrine, bathroom and installed a tube well and constructed a kitchen upon the 'kha' schedule land and has been in possession since 1976. The valuation of his construction would not he less than Tk. 2,00,000.00. The schedule Kha property was never a part and parcel of ancestral homestead of the plaintiff and defendant No. 2. There is no joint ness of the homestead of the plaintiff and of the defendant No. 2. The aid of section 4 of the Partition Act has got no manner of application and with these averments he prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

5. The plaintiff examined 3 PWs and the defendant examined 3 DWs. 

6. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit in part assessing the share of the plaintiff to the extent of 30 decimals in the ka schedule land to the plaint but dismissed the prayer made under Section 4 of the Partition Act by the judgment and decree dated 10.1.1991. 

7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 53 of 1991 and the said appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge. 1st Court, Faridpur, who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.4.1994 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment of the trial Court. 

8. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff has obtained the instant Rule. 

9. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate for the Petitioner submitted that the Courts below have committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in assessing the share of the plaintiff and also rejecting the prayer made under section 4 of the Partition Act. He submitted that admittedly plot No. 2523 is a homestead and the plot No. 2525 is the outer yard and is a part and parcel of the homestead. He submitted that some portion of land of plot No. 2523 is Matial. He submitted that the plaintiff by examining PW1, PW2. PW3 and PW4 could able to prove that the homestead constructed upon the plot No. 2525 is the ancestral undivided homestead of the plaintiff and as well as of the defendant No. 2. He submitted that the defendant No. 1 could not produce any evidence before the Court disentitling the plaintiff from getting relief under Section 4 of the Partition Act. He submitted that aid of section 4 of the partition Act is available to save a co-sharer from the disturbance of outsider in the enjoyment of undivided ancestral homestead. He submitted that admittedly the plaintiff is a Hindu by casts and the defendant is Muslim by faith and the homestead, of the plaintiff being an undivided homestead, the Courts below ought to have allowed the prayer made under section 4 of the Partition Act in view of the evidence adduced by the plaintiff in the suit. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder took me to the evidence of PWs and submitted that the Courts below have totally failed to discuss and consider the material evidence as adduced by PW 1, PW2. PW3 and PW4 so far the fact of undivided homestead is concerned, he prayed that the total land for partition being 1.33 acres and the plaintiff been an admitted co-sharers in 8 annas share the Courts below ought to have been given a preliminary decree for partition to the extent of 661/2 decimal of land and ought to have allowed the prayer for pre-emption under section 4 of the Partition Act as against the land Kha schedule land to the plaint. He prayed for an interference by this Court against the impugned judgment and decree. 

10. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin. the learned Advocate for the Opposite Parties on appearing before this Court submitted that the homestead constructed upon plot No: 2523 was not the undivided dwelling house of the plaintiff and of the defendant No. 2. He submitted that PW2 has admitted in his evidence “সুধীরের পিতার বাড়ীর উত্তর পাশে জীতেনের (বাদীর) বাড়ী দক্ষিণ পাশে।”. He further submitted that the DW3 admitted in his evidence “বাদী ও বিবাদীর বাড়ী একই প্লট। মাঝখানে ফাঁকা আছে। বেড়া চীতেন্দ্র নাথ দিয়েছে।” He further submitted that paragraph 2 of the plaint disclosed the following averments “দখলের সুবিধার জন্য বাদী ও ২নং বিবাদী পৃথক গৃহাদি উঠাইয়া স্বত্ববান ও দখলকার আছে।” He further submitted that these evidences clearly show that there is no existence of undivided homestead of the plaintiff and as well as of the defendant No. 2 in the suit land. He submitted that the Courts below on considering the evidence on record have correctly rejected the prayer for pre-emption under section 4 of the Partition Act. He further submitted that the judgment and decree impugned in the Rule being a judgment of affirmance, the same is liable to be undisturbed unless any case of non-consideration of any evidence or non-reading of any evidence or misreading of any evidence on record is made out. 

11. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and have considered their submissions. I have perused the judgments of the Courts below and the evidence on record very carefully. 

12. From paragraph 4 of the revisional application the Petitioner has made out a clear case of non-consideration of the evidence of PW2 and PW3 and in the ground No. 4 the Petitioner has taken a ground that the evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW3.were not considered by the Courts below. 

13. Since a case of total non-consideration of the evidence of the PW 1. PW2 and PW3 has been taken as ground and has been agitated before this Court, the judgment and decree although are the judgment of affirmances is yet to be looked into as to whether those were passed upon consideration of the evidence of those PWs. Although.it is the settled principle of law that a revisional Court should not disturb the concurrent finding of the Courts below but our Appellate Division in the case of Abul Bakar Siddique versus Additional Deputy Commissioner, reported in 48 DLR (A. D)-154 has given a authority to High Court Division to reassess the evidence on record where a clear case of total non-consideration of the material evidence has been made out. In the instant case the plaintiff is admittedly a co-sharer to the ka schedule land to the plaint to the extent of 8-annas share. The total land covered by Ka schedule land measures an area of 1.33 acres of land. Admittedly the plaintiff is entitled to get a preliminary decree for partition to the extent of .661/2  acres of land but the Courts below have given a preliminary decree to the extent of 30 decimals. It is nobody's case that the plaintiff has sold some property elsewhere. In view of the above the plaintiff was entitled to get a preliminary decree to the extent of .661/2 acres of land. I find that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in assessing the share of the plaintiff and the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law. The plaintiff is entitled to get a decree to the extent of 661/2, decimals in preliminary form. 

14. Now let us consider the question of pre-emption under section 4 of the Partition Act. Section 4 of the Partition Act reads as follows:- 

"4. (1) Where a share of a dwelling-house belonging to an undivided family has been transferred to a person who is not a member of such family and such transferee sues for partition. the Court shall, in any member of the family being a share-holder shall undertake to buy the share of such transferee, make a valuation of such share in such manner as it thinks fit and direct the sale of such share to such share-holder, and may give all necessary and proper directions in that behalf. 

(2) If in any case described in sub-section (1) two or more members of the family being such share-holders severally undertake to buy such share. The Court shall follow the procedure prescribed by sub-section (2) of the last foregoing section." 

15. Ongoing through the section 4 of the Partition Act it appears that if any transfer of any share of undivided family dwelling house is transferred to a person who is not a member of such family, any member of the undivided family can seek pre-emption under the said section 4 of the Partition Act. Now let us discuss the evidence of PWI, PW2, PW3 whether they could make out a case to extend the aid of section 4 of the Partition Act. The PWI is the plaintiff of the suit who in his examination-in-chief has adduced “বিরোধীয় খতিয়ানের উপরোক্ত বাড়ী আমাদের  পৈত্রিক বাড়ী। বিঃ হাল ২৫২৩ দাগে নাঃ এস, এ, ১৯৩ নং খতিয়ানের ২৫২৩ নং দাগে আমার ও ২য় নং বিবাদীর পৈত্রিক আমলের বসতবাড়ী। এস, এ, ২৭০ ও ২৭৪ নং খতিয়ানের ২৫২৫ দাগের মাটিয়াল এবং উহার বাড়ী সংলগ্ন এবং বাড়ীর অংশ।” This evidence of PWI has not been disturbed or shaken during cross-examination. The PW2 Kazi Hatim being a neighbourer of  the plaintiff in his examination-in-chief has adduced “নালিশী ভূমি পূর্বে জীতেন দাও ও সুধীর কুমার দাসের ছিল। তারা একই বাড়ীতে বাস করিত। বাড়ীর একই চৌহদ্দি।”  In cross-examination this PW2 has admitted “সুধীরের পিতার বাড়ী উত্তর পাশে এবং জীতেন দাসের বাড়ী দক্ষিণ দিকে ছিল। বর্তমানেও ১নং বাড়ীর দক্ণিষাংশে এবং উত্তর পাশে অত্র বিবাদীর বাড়ী”. This evidence has remained unshaken during cross-examination. The PW3 Babanath Das being another neighbouer of the plaintiffs village in his examination-in-chief has added:- “নালিশী ভূমির পাশে আমার বাড়ী। নালিশী জীতেন দাস এবং সুধীর দাসের পূর্ব পুরুষের আমলের বাড়ী। উক্ত বাড়ী কখনও ভাগ বাটোয়ারা হয় নাই।”  This evidence also have not been shaken during cross-examination. The DWI, it the son of the defendant No. 1 in his cross-examination has admitted “নালিশী ২৫২৩ দাগে সুধীরের বাপ দাদা বাস করিত শুনিয়াছি। ২৫২৩ দাগের দক্ষিণে ২৫২৫ দাগে মাটিয়াল। ……….. আমাদের খরিদের পূর্বে নালিশী ভূমি বাদী ২নং বিবাদীদের পূর্ববর্তী আমলীর এজমালী বসতবাড়ী ছিল কিনা জানিনা।” If this evidence of the DWI be read together with the evidence of PWs, 1-3 those proved beyond doubt that the homestead constructed upon the land of plot No. 2523 is the ancestral homestead of the plaintiff and as well as of the defendant No. 2. The Courts below keept those evidence totally out of consideration and have passed the impugned judgment. It is admitted by both the parties that there has been no partition by metes and bounds between the parties earlier. To get the aid of section 4 of the Partition Act the plaintiff in his examination-in-chief has added “আমি হিন্দু সম্প্রদায়ের এবং ১নং বিবাদী মুসলমান আমাদের জীবন যাপন সামাজিক আচার হইতে ১নং বিবাদীর সামাজিক আচার-আচরণ সম্পূর্ণ ভিন্ন। আমাদের জীবন যাপনের মধ্যে কোন প্রকার সামঞ্জস্য নাই। নালিশী ভূমি আমার পিতার আমাদের এজমালী বসতবাড়ী। ১নং বিবাদী নিজে নালিশী বাড়ীদে বসবাস করে না। ১নং বিবাদী বা তাহার পক্ষে লোকজনরে সহিত আমার বসবাস করা বম্ভব নহে। নক তাপছিলের ভূমি বন্টনক্রমে খ তফছিল বাই আপ চাহিয়া অত্র মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করিয়াছি।”This evidence were not denied by the defendant by putting any suggestion to the PW I. 

16. From the evidence as discussed above, it is proved beyond doubt the homestead upon the plot No. 2523 and the land of plot No. 2525 are the part and parcel of the ancestral homestead of the plaintiff and as well as of the defendant No. 2 and there having been no partition by metes and hounds and the defendant No. 1 being an outsider and being not a member of the plaintiffs family, the land purchased by him comes within the mischief of section 4 of the Partition Act in view of the case law reported in 40 DLR(AD) 150 and the case law reported in 42 DLR(AD) 10. The Courts below without discussing and considering material and important evidence have rejected the claim of the plaintiff. The same is not sustainable in law and is liable to be set aside by this Court. 

17. On perusal of the record, it appears, that during trial of the suit, an advocate commissioner was appointed for assessing the valuation of the structures as raised by the defendant No. 1 upon the suit land and the learned Advocate Commissioner submitted his report before the Court on 5.9.1984. It further appears that no objection was submitted by the plaintiff as against the said report. The Advocate Commissioner was examined on 30.7.1986 and that report was accepted by order No. 102 dated 23.2.1988. From the said report it appears that the costs incurred towards the constructions of the structures as raised by the defendant No. 1 was worth about Tk. 40,000.00. 

18. It is very important to note that the defendant No.1 himself did not come forward to deny the plaintiffs case and to dispose before the Court. His son was examined as DW1 without getting any authority from him to dispose. The case of the plaintiff remained undented by the defendant. From the fact and circumstances and discussions made above, 1 hold that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in dismissing the plaintiffs appeal. He further submits that agreement 'dated 19.12.1990 has became legally unenforceable. because the respondent has refused to pay the balance money in order to execute a sale deed, rather he had frequently asked to return the earnest money and thus violated the terms and conditions of the agreement dated 19.12.1990 and that the agreement lost its legal enforceability that the agreement lost its legal enforceability as soon as the respondent refused to pay the balance money and asked for the repayment of earnest money. 

16. Mr. Md. Moinul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate further submits that the trial court was wrong in not considering that the .respondent filed the suit in order to harass and cause Huqe amount of financial .loss to the appellants and that the appellants having produced unimpeachable evidence to that the respondent has deliberately failed to comply with the terms and' conditions of  the agreement dated 19.12.1990 upon paying the balance amount of Taka 12,28,000/= -.before execution and registration of the sale deed within 15 days or within a limited period and the trial court upon a  completely erroneous premises wrongly decreed the suit. 

17. Mr. Chowdhury the learned Advocate for the appellants cited .the decision in the case Rash Behari Moshalkar Vs. Hiron Bala Debi and another reported in 1985 BLD. (AD) 51 and the case of Silver Estate Ltd. Vs. Abdul Hakim Miah and others reported in 43 DLR 360 in support of their contention. 

18. Mr. Chowdhury the learned Advocate for the appellants further cited the decision :in the case of Rash Behari Mashlker Vs, Hiron Bala Debi and others 1985 BLD (AD) 51 and in the case of Rakhal Dasi Ranjakini Vs. Ayesha Khatoon Chowdhury and another in 1985 BLD (AD) 49 in support of his contention. 

19. Mr. 1-7. R. M. Nazmul Ashan, the learned advocate for the respondent submits that the plaintiff filed the suit for specific performance of contract directing the defendants to execute and register the sale deed in respect of suit land in favour of the respondent according to the agreement dated 19.12.1990 but the appellant failed to execute the sale deed inspite of repeated request; that the respondent served legal notice upon the appellants and having receiving notices upon the appellants came to the office of the respondent and. requested him not to file any case and also promised to execute arid register the sale deed immediately after getting the documents from the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Savar and that the respondent believed the appellants and waited for response but the appellants did not give any information and also failed to execute .a sale deed. He further submits that the respondent served legal notice through lawyer to the appellants requesting them to execute and register the sale deed on receipt of the balance money of Taka -12,28,000/= from the respondent within in 3 days from the date of receipt of the notice but the appellants failed to do so and thereby the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit. 


20. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge considering all  the material aspect of the case and evidence on record rightly decreed the suit assigning cogent and good reason as such the impugned Judgment passed by the learned subordinate Judge does not suffer any illegality or legal infirmity so as to calling for interference by this court. 

21. Now the point for determination is whether the learned Subordinate Judge is justified in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 31.01.2000. 

22. The learned Advocate for the appellant has placed before us the plaint, written statement and documents submitted by the respective parties. 

23. In a suit for specific performance of contract, court is to see whether the parties have performed their respective part. 

24. Here in this case, the agreement exhibit between the parties is admitted. The agreement was executed on 19.12.1990. The consideration money was fixed at Taka 15,28,000/ out of which Taka 3,00,000/= was paid on the day of execution of was w agreement. The terms of the agreement as that the defendants are to execute and register the sale deed arranging necessary documents failing which the plaintiff is to get the sale deed executed and registered through court 

25. The case of the plaintiff is that he requested the defendants within time to execute and register the sale deed but the defendants claimed excess price beyond the consideration money fixed at the time of execution of the agreement. Thereafter the plaintiff served legal notice upon the defendants to execute and register the sale deed but the defendants failed to do so and thus the plaintiff was bound to file suit being no. 99 of 1998 on 31.03.1998. 

26. On the other hand, the defendant's case is that the defendants executed an agreement to sell the suit land to the plaintiff for an urgent need of money but due to the failure of the plaintiff to pay the balance amount of money within the stipulated time, the plaintiff could not execute and register the sale deed. Instead, the plaintiff served legal notice to return the earnest money and threatened the defendants to take civil or criminal actions if they failed to return the earnest money. It is further stated that the defendants giving notice on 09.01.1992 specified the time to execute and register a sale deed paying balance consideration money otherwise the advance money would be forfeited but the plaintiff nether made any payment nor gave any satisfactory explanation  

27. The burden of proof is envisages in section 101 of the Evidence Act is that the burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. This rule of convenience has been adopted in practice not because it is impossible to prove a negative; but because the negative does not admit of - the direct and simple proof of which the affirmative is capable. Moreover, it is but reasonable and just than suitor who relies upon the existence of a fact, should be called upon to prove his own case. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must in order to success establish a prima facie case. He cannot on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary’s case. He must succeed by the strength of his won right and the clearness of his own proof. There is clear term of the agreement dated 19.12.1990 that the defendants are to execute and register the sale deed within 15 days of the date of agreement i.e. on or before 03.01.1991 arranging necessary documents. 

28. In the instant case, it is the contention of the respondent that the appellants failed to execute and register the sale deed within stipulated time has no legal value unless the same is substantiated by cogent and reliable evidence. Now let us see how far the contention of the respondent has been proved by cogent and credible evidence. The plaintiff respondent has examined 2 witnesses, P. W. 1 is Sakander Ali Howlader and P. W. 2 is Abdul Mannan. P. W. 1 Sakender Ali Howlader deposed that the agreement was executed on 19.12.1990. He proved the agreement which is marked as exhibit-1 and also proved the acknowledgment receipt of the taking money by the defendants respondents which is marked exhihit2. He deposed that terms of the agreement shows that while the appellants defendants failed to execute and register the sale deed within 15 days the respondent will get the kabala registered through court. He further deposed that the appellant did not execute and register the -sale deed for which he served the legal notice upon the defendants appellants, but the notice upon the defendants appellants, but they told him that if he would not give them some excess money than what is fixed in the agreement, they would not execute and register-ate sale deed. He admitted in his deposition that he saw some papers in respect of the suit land with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 when they came to his office to execute agreement and that the agreement was written seeing the photocopy of the original deeds of defendants Nos. 1 to 3. He further admitted that when the defendants appellants failed to execute and register the sale deed within time then he asked them to return the earnest money. 

29. P. W. 2, Abdul Mannan, deposed that he was present at the time of execution of the agreement and he identified his signature in the agreement which is marked as exhibit- 4 (Ka). 

30. From the evidence of their two PWs, it has not been proved that the plaintiff-respondent tendered the defendants respondents to take balance money and to execute and register the sale deed nor has it proved that defendants appellants demanded excess money than that of the fixed amount. 

31. On the contrary, it has been proved from the evidence of D.Ws that the plaintiff respondent willfully delayed to execute the -sale deed disregarding the repeated requests of the defendants- appellants. Rather it is admitted that the plaintiff- appellant asked the defendants respondents to return the earnest money and even posed himself as the real owner of the suit land giving advertisement in the daily News paper. 

32. More so the defendants also examined 2 witnesses DW-1, Mohammad All Miah, who is also defendant No.1 who deposed that the  agreement was executed on 19.12.1990; that the terms of the agreement is that if the defendant failed to execute and register the sale deed within 15 days, the plaintiff would get the kabala registered through court. He further deposed that he gave the original papers to the plaintiff from which he took the photo copies and returned the original to the defendants; that he asked the plaintiff to pay the balance money and to execute and register the sale deed but the plaintiff did not pay the money for which they served the legal notice to the plaintiff which is marked as exhibit Ka. He denied the suggestion that he did not execute and register the sale deed due to enhancement of the price of suit land. He further deposed that they price of suit land. He further deposed that they are in possession of the suit land. 

33. D. W.- 2, Abdul Aziz, deposed that he knew the plaintiff and the defendants and  testified that he was present at time of the examination of the agreement dated 19.12.1990 and the terms of agreement was that if the defendants failed to execute and register the sale .deed within 15 days, the plaintiff will get the kabala registered through the court by filing suit for specific Performance of contract. He further deposed that the original papers were given to the plaintiff and that the plaintiff was requested in his presence to pay them the balance consideration money and to execute and register the sale deed but the plaintiff failed to do so and rather he asked the defendants to return the earnest money. 

34. He further proved the documents filed by the defendants which are marked as exhibits-- Ka. Kha, Oma. 

35. From the evidence of D.Ws it has also been proved that the plaintiffs did not execute and register sale deed within time in spite of the repeated requests from the side of the defendants rather the plaintiffs threatened to return the earnest money and illegally posed himself as the owner of the suit property. 

36. As per Article 113 of the limitation Act, the plaintiff is to file the suit for specific performance of contract within 3 years from the date of expiry or the date of refusal. In the instant case, the agreement was executed on 19.12.1990. The term of the agreement was that the plaintiff is to execute and -register the sale deed within 15 days getting the rest consideration' money. It has been proved that the plaintiff neither tendered balance consideration money nor did he file the suit for specific performance of contract within time. The plaintiff has also totally failed to prove the factum of refusal by the defendants. 15 days from the date of execution of the agreement dated 19.12.1990 stands on 04.01.1991 and 3 years from 04.01.1994 Stands on 04.01.1994. The plaintiff ought to have file suit for specific performance of contract within 04.01.1994 but the plaintiff filed the suit on 31.02.1998 that is he has filed the suit long after 4 years 2 months and 9 days of the statutory period of limitation. The plaintiff have totally failed to prove the caused of delay, rather it have been proved that the plaintiff threatened the defendants to return the earnest money and sometime posing himself to be the owners of the suit land by advertising in the daily News paper. Thus the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. 

37. The very pathetic sinariao of this case is that the defendants are very poor and illiterate persons who intended to sell the suit land in need of money but the plaintiff, who is rich man harassed the defendants enormously in different ways not giving the balance consideration money, rather illegally pressurized them to return the earnest money and even the plaintiff lodged diary in the police station against the defendants. More curiously the plaintiff claimed himself openly as the owners of the suit land through advertisement the News paper. All these illegal activities of the plaintiff debarred' him from getting any discretion from the court.  

38. It is undoubted rule that the court can exercise discretion in a suit for Specific performance of contract. But it does not mean that it is .open to a court to do just what it pleases in an individual case without regard to authority or principle, Granting a specific performance is not to be claimed as matter of right. It is in the discretion of the court and will not be done unless complete justice can be done by the party seeking it. Discretionary is not arbitrary or capricious but it must be regulated upon grounds that would make it judicial. No hard and fast rules can be laid down. In exercising its discretionary power a court will grant or withhold relief according to the case presented. In every case the question must be whether the exercise of the power of the court is demanded to sub- serve the ends of justice and unless the court is satisfied that it is right in every respect it refuses to interfere. 

39. The senariao of this case clearly shown that the plaintiff has harassed the defendants in different ways narrated above and has deprived them from getting balance money in time of need inspite repeated requests and legal notice and ultimately instituted suit long after 4 years 2 months 9 days of the statutory period . of Limitation without explaining satisfactory ground of delay in filing suit. In such circumstances the plaintiff is not legally entitled to get any discretion from the court 

40. The essence of specific performance is that each party has its specific part to be performed. If any party of the contract fails to perform his obligation he will not get relief. In the instant case the plaintiff has totally failed to perform his obligation. So he is not entitled to get any relief in his time barred suit 1 

41. In the case of Jaggo Bai Vs. Hari Har Prosad Sing reported in PLD 1947 PC it has been held' by the Privy Council that the " plaintiff is entitled to get reasonable interest on the earnest money. Agreeing with the views expressed in the aforesaid decisions, we hold that the plaintiff is entitled to get interest in the prevalent bank rate till realization in case of failure to pay the earnest money within time fixed by the court. 
Considering the fact and circumstances of the case and evidence on record we are Of 47,1 the view that the plaintiff totally failed to prove his case and there is merit in this appeal. 

42. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree dated 31.01.2000 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 4th court and Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka is set aside.

43. The connected Rule is also disposed of setting aside the order of stay.  

44. The defendants appellant are directed refund the earnest money of Taka 3.00,000/ the plaintiff respondent within 4(four) months from the date, failing which interest at the rate of 15% per annum will be charged upon this amount from the date of decree-till realization. 
Send down the L.C.R at once.

	End.

 4. The case of the defendants 1 & 2 is that the defendant No.1 is a contractor and opened an account in the plaintiff bank for his business purpose and he developed intimacy with defendant No.3 the former manager 'of the Bank who used to advice him in business matters and he signed some blank papers when took loan of Tk. 50,000/-which were converted to the present documents,. 8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and. decree dismissing the suit against the defendants 1 & 2 the plaintiff as appellant has filed the present appeal. 

9. Mr. M.A. Tariq, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that the trial court committed gross error in failing to hold that amount in question was withdrawn from the account of the defendant No. 1 & 2 are also jointly and severally liable for the amount in question along with the defendant No. 3 Mr. Tariq submits that upon a correct reading Of the evidence, both oral and documentary, decree may be passed as against the defendants I & 2 also making them liable jointly and severally to repay the bank money. 

10. No. one entered appearance on behalf of the respondents though notices of the appeal were duly served on them as appears or the office note dated 14.07.93. 

11. We have considered the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant and perused the pleadings of the parties and the evidence on record. There is no dispute with regard to excess drawing of an amount of Tk. 2,67,000/- from the account of the defendant No.l. The defendants 1 & 2 as Stated that the defended No.3 was responsible for the said over drawing while the defendant No. 3 alleged that the defendants 1 & 2 are responsible for the said over drawing. We are therefore required to find out as to who is responsible for the overdrawing of the amount in. question on the bails of the evidence available record. 

12. The plaintiff examined one Bibekananda Biswas, Manager of the Bank as P.W.1 who has proved the plaintiffs case as made out in the plaintiff and also proved all the documents which were marked Exts. 1-6. All the documents proved by the P.W. relate to Cash Credit Loan of Tk.50.000/- and withdrawal of money by cheque dated 25.09.65 for an amount of Tk. 82,000/-, cheque dated 31.08.65 for an amount of Tk. 90,000/-, cheque dated 31.4.85 for an amount of Tk. 95,000/- By these cheques in all of Tk.2,67,000/- was withdrawn by way of excess drawing . The defendants 1 & 2 specifically asserted in the written statement that there was a salish held in the house of the superintendent krishnapour Aliya Madrasha on 23.10.85 where the defendant No. 3 admitted in presence of several persons that he had withdrawn Tk.2,67,000/- from the account of the defendant Nos. 1&2 and also another amount of Tk. 2,60,400/-from the account of the brother of the defendant No.1 and Nurul Amin and admitted in presence of the salish to pay' entire amount to the bank within January, 1986 and that the said defendant No. 3 executed an undertaking on 29-10-85 sitting in his house in presence of witnesses. The defendant No.1 examined himself as P.W.1 and stated in his evidence that he had kept signed blank cheques with defendant No. 3 with the bonafide belief as there was no arrangement for any over drawing. He also stated that the instructed the Manager that whenever he would send messenger, the Manager may withdraw the amount chaque using his singed cheques so that he could run his business D.W. 1 also stated that the defendant No. 3 withdrew Tk. 2,67,000/- by way of over drawing from his account using his signed cheque. D.W. 1 further stated that there was a salish on 28.10.85 in the house of the principal of Krishnapur Aliya Madrasha and the defendant No.3 admitted withdrawn of money before the Salishdars and assured that he shall deposit the said amount in the account D.W 1 also stated that the defendant No. 3 executed an undertaking in the stamp paper on 29-10-85 admitting the over drawings and also under taking to deposit the entire amount in the bank's account of the defendant No. 1 and his brother Nurul Amin. 

13. We have plerused the cheques Exts.15,15(19) and 15 (kha) by which a total amount of Tk. 2,67,000/- was withdrawn. From the seal appearing in Ext, 15, 15 (ka) and 15(kha) we find signature of the Manager of the Bank, Motin who is defendant No.3. We have perused the under taking Ext. Kha dated 29.1085 signed by defendant No, 3 who examined himself as D.W. 1 for defendant No. 3 and denied excess drawing or drawing of any amount from the account of defendant No. 1 D. W. 1 Abdul Motin also stated in his evidence that the defendant No 1 Nurul Islam and his brought Nurul Amin brother a stamp paper worth Tk.3/- in presence of the police & obtained his signature thereon. D.W. 1 stated that Ext. Kha was created on the said stamp D.W. 1 state in his cross-examination by the plaintiff that there was no provision of over drawing. In the sanction letter and admitted that he was dismissed from service for excess drawing In his cross examination by defendants 1 & 2 D. W.1 A Motin stated that his signature was taken by force on stamp paper in presence of the principal but he did not ledge any G.D. Entry or made any grievance to any one for obtaining his signature by force .He denied that the signature was not taken by force, He admitted that the charge sheet has been submitted against him for excess drawing. 

14. We have considered the evidence of D.W.1, undertaking Ext. Kha and It appears to us that the defendant No. 3 did not deny his signature on the undertaking but alleged that his signature was obtained by force. It appears that he did not inform any one about the obtaining his signature by force or did not lodge any G.D. Entry with the police Station D.W.3 was serving in a bank as a Manager and discharging a responsible job and he must- have known the import of taking. his signature by force as alleged by him, D.W.3 has not examined any witness to corroborate him that his signature was taken by force. Even he did not examine anyone to prove in whose presence his signature was obtained by force. One Rokanuddin, a principal of Krishnapur Aliya Madrasha was examined as D.W. 2 and he stated in his evidence about the salish in October,1985 in respect of Bank's transaction and the defendant No. 3 Motin Shaheb admitted that 40, he took loan of Tk. 2,67,000/- from the account of the defendant No.1 and another amount of Tk. 2,61,000/- from the account of the brother of defendant No.1 Nurul Amin and that the undertaking was executed on the following day D.W.2 also stated that he was present when the undertaking was executed by defendant No. 3 and he become a witness to the said undertaking. 

15. We have considered the evidence of D.W. 2 and we find that he was a witness to the under taking Ext. Kha The defendant also, examined one Md. Mozibur Rahman as D.W. 3 who was a Teacher of the said Madrasha and of the scribe of the undertaking of Ext. Kha D.W. 3 stated in his evidence that there was a salish in the house of principal and that he was present in the Salish he also stated that the salish took place on 28.10.85 and that the defendant No. 3 admitted that he had withdrawn total amount of Tk.5,35,000/- from the account of the defendant No. 1 Nurul Islam and his brother Nurul Amin and also agreed to repay the said amount within 31.1.86. The stated that he wrote ext. Kha. 

16. On a perusal of the evidence of D.W. 1 and 2 along with the evidence of defendant No.3 we do not find any reason to disbelieve the genuineness of Ext. Kha. We also do not find any reason to disbelieve of the evidence D.W. 1 and 2 Md. Rokanuddin And Md. Mozibur Rahman who has neither any relationship nor any enmity was suggested by the defendant No. 3 we therefore find that the signature of defendant No. 1 appearing in Exts. 15 (Ka) and 15 (Kha) has been successfully explained Having considered the facts of the case and the evidence on record including Ext. Kha we are of the view that the trial court has arrived at a correct conclusion holding that the defendant No.3 alone was responsible for the overdrawing and no cognent reason could be pointed out to discard the finding of the trial Court. Apart from other evidence Ext. kha alone is sufficient to find that the defendant No. 3 alone was responsible for the overdrawing of the amount in question. It is record that the defendant No. 3 Who was the Manager of the Bank at the relevant time had no authority to grant any over drawing to any account holders or to any customer. On a consideration of the cheques Ext. 15 (Ka) and 15 (Kha) we find that the entire amount of Tk. 2,67,000/- was with' drawn by the cheques on two dates and that could be possible by defendant No. 3 being the manager of the Bank inasmuch as we find seals in all the cheques and signature of the Manager alone and none else. Withdrawal of over Tk. 10,000/- must be verified by 2(two) officers in discharging normal parties in banking matters and at the relevant time a period 7 days notice was required to be submitted to the bank for drawing over Tk. 10,000/- We do not find any such application or notice in the instant case. The chaeques contained the signature of the account holder but explanation assigned by the account-holder appears to be reasonable. We, therefore, do not find any reason to disagree with the finding arrived at by the trial Court holding that the defendant No.3 alone was liable for the overdrawing of the amount in question. We do not therefore find any substance in the submissions, made by the learned Advocate for the appellant. 

17. For the forgoing reasons, this appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 19.2.91 passed by the subordinate judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Mymensingh in Money Suit No:45 of 1990 are nearby affirmed. Send down the lower court records at once.
